title: Political Development, Decay, and Civic Culture

scenes.text: Can a country have vibrant elections but still face political decay?
scenes.narration: Imagine a country where millions vote enthusiastically, yet the government struggles to enforce basic laws. Can high voter turnout actually lead to political decay?

scenes.text: A school cricket club admitting hundreds of players without bats, pitches, or umpires.
scenes.narration: Think of this analogy: your school sports club recruits hundreds of eager players, but has only two broken bats and no referee. Without strong management to handle the crowd, enthusiasm turns into total chaos.

scenes.heading: Pye's Three Development Parameters
items: Equality: High political participation across society
Capacity: State power to enforce laws firmly
Differentiation: Specialized bodies for every function
scenes.narration: Scholar Lucian Pye explained that political development is different from economic wealth. It needs three pillars: equality through participation, state capacity to enforce laws, and specialized institutions for each task.

scenes.heading: Huntington's Political Decay
scenes.narration: Samuel Huntington warned of political decay when mass participation grows faster than institutions can adapt. In places like India from the 1970s, rising demands overwhelmed unadaptable systems.

scenes.heading: Path of Political Modernisation
scenes.narration: To avoid western bias, David Apter and Huntington proposed looking at modernisation. They believed shifts like urbanisation and rationalisation mobilise people, build nations, and naturally foster democracy.

scenes.heading: Three Types of Political Culture
scenes.narration: Gabriel Almond and Sydney Verba studied political culture, meaning people's shared values toward politics. They mapped three types: parochial who remain indifferent, subjects who merely obey policies, and participants who actively shape decisions.

scenes.heading: The Balanced Civic Culture
items: Combines participant, subject, and parochial cultures
Prevents demagogues like Hitler in Germany
scenes.narration: Here is the secret: Almond and Verba found that stable democracy needs a civic culture. You need mostly active participants, but also enough patient subjects so extreme passions do not breed dictators like Hitler.

items: Pye measured equality, state capacity, and differentiation.
Huntington showed participation without institutions causes decay.
Almond and Verba proved civic culture stabilizes democracy.
scenes.narration: To recap: first, development demands state capacity, not just voting. Second, weak institutions facing huge demands suffer decay. And third, a balanced civic culture keeps democracy peaceful and stable.
